text: The authors fine-tune large language models with behavioural cloning to write natural-language critiques, and report that on topic-based summarisation these critiques help humans find flaws they would otherwise miss, both naturally occurring flaws in model- and human-written summaries and intentional flaws in deliberately misleading human summaries. They report that larger models write more helpful critiques, are on most tasks better at self-critiquing despite harder-to-critique outputs, and can use their own self-critiques to refine their summaries.
title: Self-critiquing models: model-written critiques help humans find flaws in summaries
